findings.title: Fake disabled IDs bypass the existing castId-only structural control
findings.scenario: Four client query builders manufacture empty branded IDs so disabled query keys typecheck. If an enabled guard drifts, an invalid ID reaches tRPC and becomes a user-visible query failure. The existing no-fake-disabled-id gate resolves only canonical castId calls, so these direct assertions are invisible.
findings.repairGroup: Represent absence with null/skipToken or the existing gated query helper, then extend the semantic reader to checker-resolved nonbrand-to-brand assertions with a static empty value. Do not key it on the spelling as ChatId.

findings.title: BroadcastChannel parsing claims an unvalidated string is a Handle
findings.scenario: A same-origin extension or stale tab can post session-recovered with an empty/arbitrary handle. asSessionMessage returns a SessionMessage carrying Handle even though it only checked typeof string. Today the value is compared and a mismatch hard-reloads, so this is a type-contract lie rather than an identity takeover.

evidence.fact: typeof string followed by handle as Handle
value is comparison-only and mismatch reloads

findings.repairGroup: Parse with the canonical Handle schema or keep the decoded channel field string until comparison; preserve the fail-closed reload behavior.

findings.title: The AppRouter client bridge is compile-time-only on outputs
findings.scenario: Inputs have 365 .input parsers across 425 procedures, but the router tree has zero .output parsers. HTTP JSON is decoded by tRPC and accepted by the client under the inferred AppRouter output type. A malformed DB projection or server regression therefore crosses as a stronger client type without a runtime output contract.
findings.repairGroup: First build a semantic inventory of procedure outputs and classify which are already constructed from parsed contracts or constrained DB rows. Add output schemas only at untrusted/projection seams; do not blanket duplicate every domain result.
